decisions.reason: Product A has a dedicated webpage and an announced US release in Q1/2019, indicating visible commitment and a temporary geographic delay rather than fundamental failure.
Product B has its own webpage and belongs to the firm's announced dosimetry portfolio, so sunk investments and public commitment favor keeping it.
Product C is publicly listed and part of the firm's strategic QA offering, making early slow uptake attributable to temporary market development.
Product D appears on a dedicated page and fits the firm's integrated dosimetry direction, so management is likely to persist rather than write off the launch investment.
Product E is part of the newly launched ionization chamber line with public visibility, and no permanent disappointing results are reported, favoring continuation.
Product F has a public product page and completes the firm's new chamber portfolio, so dropping it would undercut the announced product family and incurred costs.
